Course Project · ENES220

Wooden I-Beam Design & Optimization

Derived failure-load equations and built a Python optimizer to balance three failure modes for an asymmetric pine I-beam.

Course: ENES220 — Mechanics of Materials

Team: 6 members

My role: Derived the governing equations and wrote the optimization code

Problem

Design an I-beam cross-section from pine lumber and wood glue that maximizes load-carrying capacity. The beam has an asymmetric cross-section and can fail through three distinct mechanisms: flexural failure (bending stress), wood shear failure, and glue-joint shear failure.

Approach

I derived the stress and failure-load equations for all three failure modes from first principles (neutral axis location, moment of inertia, shear flow). The key insight was that the optimal beam should have all three failure loads as close to each other as possible — if one mode is much weaker than the others, material is wasted reinforcing modes that won't govern.

I wrote a Python optimizer that parameterized the cross-section dimensions and iteratively searched for a geometry where the three failure loads were balanced within 20% of each other. The team then built the beam and tested it to failure in the lab.
